description: Category boards. Each board has categories, each with clues at rising point values. The player picks a cell, reads the clue, and types the answer (the 'in the form of a question' phrasing is accepted but not required). Every clue carries an authoritative citation.

clues.clue: The gateway to the other sacraments, it frees from original sin and makes one a member of the Church.
clues.explanation: Baptism regenerates the person as a child of God and cannot be repeated.

clues.clue: This sacrament seals the baptized with the Gift of the Holy Spirit and completes baptismal grace.
clues.explanation: Confirmation more perfectly binds the Christian to the Church and strengthens them for witness.

clues.clue: Also called Penance and Confession, this sacrament restores a person to grace after grave sin.
clues.explanation: Through the priest's absolution God grants pardon and peace to the contrite sinner.

clues.clue: God set a rainbow in the sky as the sign of His covenant with this man after the flood.
clues.explanation: The covenant with Noah remains in force as long as the world lasts, embracing all living creatures.

clues.clue: At this mountain Moses received the Law, and the covenant was sealed with the blood of sacrifice.
clues.explanation: The Sinai covenant made Israel a priestly people belonging to God.

clues.clue: God promised this king that his throne and his house would be established forever, a promise fulfilled in Christ.
clues.explanation: The everlasting kingdom promised to David is realized in the reign of his descendant, the Messiah.

clues.clue: The Creed professed at Sunday Mass takes its name from councils held in 325 and 381.
clues.explanation: It draws on the great councils of Nicaea and Constantinople and is common to East and West.

clues.clue: Added at Nicaea, this term means 'of the same substance' and affirms that the Son is fully God.
clues.explanation: Against Arius, Nicaea confessed the Son as consubstantial with the Father.

clues.clue: The Creed names these four marks of the Church.
acceptedAnswers: What are one, holy, catholic, and apostolic
clues.explanation: These four inseparable marks identify the Church Christ founded.

clues.clue: The Lord taught this prayer of seven petitions when the disciples asked Him how to pray.
clues.explanation: The Catechism calls the Lord's Prayer the summary of the whole Gospel.

clues.clue: One of the three major expressions of prayer, it rests wordlessly in God's presence, a 'gaze of faith.'
clues.explanation: Contemplative prayer is a silent love that keeps its eyes fixed on Jesus.

clues.clue: This Old Testament book of 150 prayers is prayed daily by the Church in the Liturgy of the Hours.
clues.explanation: The Psalms are the masterwork of prayer in the Old Testament and remain the Church's own.

clues.clue: This bishop of Hippo wrote the Confessions and The City of God.
clues.explanation: Augustine is among the most influential of the Western Fathers and Doctors of the Church.

clues.clue: The Angelic Doctor, this Dominican wrote the Summa Theologiae and the Corpus Christi hymns.
clues.explanation: The Catechism quotes Aquinas's Eucharistic hymn Adoro te devote.

clues.clue: This deacon and later bishop of Alexandria stood almost alone against Arianism and was exiled five times.
clues.explanation: Athanasius defended the Nicene confession of Christ's full divinity through decades of exile.

clues.clue: The Mass has two principal parts: the Liturgy of the Word and this.
acceptedAnswers: What is the Liturgy of the Eucharist
clues.explanation: Word and Eucharist together form one single act of worship.

clues.clue: The change of the whole substance of bread and wine into Christ's Body and Blood is called this.
clues.explanation: The appearances of bread and wine remain, but the reality is now Christ Himself.

clues.clue: The Mass is not a new sacrifice but the making-present of this one event.
acceptedAnswers: What is the sacrifice of the Cross
clues.explanation: The Eucharist re-presents the one sacrifice of Calvary and applies its fruit.

clues.clue: This dogma holds that Mary, from the first instant of her conception, was preserved free from original sin.
clues.explanation: Mary was preserved immaculate by a singular grace, in view of the merits of Christ.

clues.clue: At the end of her earthly life, Mary was taken body and soul into heavenly glory; this is called her ___.
clues.explanation: The Assumption is a singular sharing in her Son's Resurrection and anticipates the glory of all the redeemed.

clues.clue: The Council of Ephesus in 431 defended this title of Mary, meaning 'God-bearer.'
clues.explanation: Because her Son is one divine person, Mary is truly Mother of God.

clues.clue: The four last things are death, judgment, heaven, and this.
clues.explanation: Hell is the state of definitive self-exclusion from communion with God.

clues.clue: This is the final purification of those who die in God's grace but are still imperfectly purified.
clues.explanation: The purification of purgatory is entirely different from the punishment of the damned.

clues.clue: At the end of time Christ returns in glory and all the dead rise for this event.
clues.explanation: The Last Judgment reveals the ultimate meaning of the whole work of creation and salvation.

clues.clue: This council of 325 gave the Creed the word 'consubstantial' and condemned the priest Arius.
clues.explanation: Nicaea confessed the Son as true God from true God, of one substance with the Father.

clues.clue: This council of 451 defined that Christ is one divine person in two natures, human and divine, unconfused and undivided.
clues.explanation: Chalcedon safeguarded both the full humanity and full divinity of the one Christ.

clues.clue: This council, held from 1962 to 1965, produced Lumen Gentium and Sacrosanctum Concilium.
acceptedAnswers: What is the Second Vatican Council
clues.explanation: Vatican II renewed the Church's self-understanding and its liturgy without changing the deposit of faith.

clues.clue: This heresy taught that the Son is the highest creature but not truly God.
clues.explanation: Against Arius, the Church confessed the Son as consubstantial with the Father.

clues.clue: From a Greek word for 'to seem,' this early error denied that Christ had a real human body and really suffered.
clues.explanation: The first heresies denied not so much Christ's divinity as his true humanity.

clues.clue: Condemned at Ephesus in 431, this held that Mary is mother only of the human Christ, so she should not be called 'Mother of God.'
clues.explanation: Because her Son is one divine person, Mary is truly the Mother of God (Theotokos).

clues.clue: This council, 1545 to 1563, answered the Protestant Reformation and reformed Church discipline.
acceptedAnswers: What is the Council of Trent
clues.explanation: Trent clarified doctrine on Scripture, justification, and the sacraments, and reformed clergy formation.

clues.clue: Trent affirmed that Christ instituted exactly this many sacraments.
clues.explanation: The seven sacraments touch all the stages and important moments of Christian life.

clues.clue: The Catechism acknowledges that from the Church's beginnings 'certain rifts' arose, wounding this unity Christ willed.
acceptedAnswers: What is the unity of the Church
clues.explanation: Divisions among Christians contradict Christ's will; the movement to restore unity is called ecumenism.

clues.clue: The Church is 'one' because its source is the unity of this.
clues.explanation: The Church's unity flows from and images the unity of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

clues.clue: The Church is 'catholic' — meaning universal — because it has the fullness of Christ and is sent to these.
clues.explanation: Catholicity means the Church carries the whole faith to the whole world.

clues.clue: The Church is 'apostolic' because it is founded on these and hands on their teaching.
clues.explanation: The Church keeps the teaching of the apostles and is guided by their successors, the bishops.

clues.clue: The first book of the Bible, telling of creation, the fall, and the flood.
clues.explanation: Genesis lays the foundation: God creates freely and well, and humanity falls.

clues.clue: In this book Israel is delivered from Egypt and receives the Law at Sinai.
clues.explanation: The Exodus is the founding act of God's covenant with Israel.

clues.clue: Its name means 'second law'; it is Moses' farewell address on the plains of Moab, and contains the Shema.
clues.explanation: Deuteronomy calls each generation to renew the covenant as if it stood at Sinai itself.

clues.clue: This Gospel, written for a Jewish-Christian audience, opens with a genealogy 'of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.'
clues.explanation: Matthew presents Jesus as the promised Messiah and new Moses.

clues.clue: The shortest and most fast-paced Gospel, traditionally linked to the preaching of Peter in Rome.
clues.explanation: Mark drives toward the cross and the centurion's confession that Jesus is the Son of God.

clues.clue: This Gospel alone opens with the prologue 'In the beginning was the Word.'
clues.explanation: John proclaims the eternal Word made flesh and full of grace and truth.

clues.clue: Paul's longest letter, to the Christians in the imperial capital, on righteousness through faith.
clues.explanation: Romans is Paul's fullest account of the gospel of grace for Jew and Gentile alike.

clues.clue: This letter contains the hymn to love: 'Love is patient, love is kind.'
clues.explanation: Chapter 13 sets charity above every gift and every work.

clues.clue: Written from prison, this letter has the hymn 'he emptied himself, taking the form of a slave.'
clues.explanation: The Christ-hymn of Philippians 2 traces the descent and exaltation of the Lord.

clues.clue: Scripture and this form one sacred deposit of the word of God, from a single divine wellspring.
clues.explanation: Scripture and Tradition are to be accepted and honored with equal devotion and reverence.

clues.clue: This Latin translation of the whole Bible was made largely by St. Jerome and became the Church's standard text.
clues.explanation: Jerome's warning still stands: ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.

clues.clue: The complete list of the 73 books the Church holds as inspired Scripture is called this.
acceptedAnswers: What is the canon of Scripture
clues.explanation: The canon was discerned by apostolic Tradition and settled definitively by the Church.

clues.clue: This fisherman was given a new name meaning 'rock' and the keys of the kingdom.
clues.explanation: On Peter and his successors Christ builds and governs His Church.

clues.clue: This apostle would not believe until he saw the wounds, then confessed 'My Lord and my God.'
clues.explanation: Thomas's confession is one of Scripture's clearest professions of Christ's divinity.

clues.clue: This tax collector rose from his customs post at a single word and is credited with the first Gospel.
clues.explanation: Matthew left everything to follow the Lord who came to call sinners.

clues.clue: This deacon, the Church's first martyr, was stoned while praying for his killers.
clues.explanation: Stephen's death, forgiving his persecutors, echoes Christ's own.

clues.clue: This Polish Franciscan took a condemned stranger's place in the Auschwitz starvation bunker.
clues.explanation: Kolbe's offering fulfills the Lord's word that no love is greater than to lay down one's life.

clues.clue: This English Lord Chancellor was beheaded for refusing to accept the king as head of the Church.
clues.explanation: More died 'the king's good servant, but God's first,' witnessing to conscience bound by truth.

clues.clue: This bishop of Hippo, converted after a wayward youth, wrote the Confessions.
clues.explanation: Augustine's restless-heart prayer opens the Catechism's treatment of prayer.

clues.clue: The 'Angelic Doctor,' this Dominican wrote the Summa Theologiae and the Corpus Christi hymns.
clues.explanation: The Catechism quotes Aquinas's Eucharistic hymn Adoro te devote.

clues.clue: The 'Little Flower,' this Carmelite taught a 'little way' and is a Doctor though she died at twenty-four.
clues.explanation: The Catechism quotes Thérèse's definition of prayer as a surge of the heart toward God.

clues.clue: This saint of Assisi founded the Friars Minor and received the wounds of Christ.
clues.explanation: Francis's poverty and love of creation as God's gift made him one of the most beloved saints.

clues.clue: Wounded by a cannonball, this soldier founded the Society of Jesus and wrote the Spiritual Exercises.
clues.explanation: Ignatius turned a soldier's discipline toward the greater glory of God.

clues.clue: This monk of Nursia wrote a Rule summed up as 'pray and work' and is the father of Western monasticism.
clues.explanation: Benedict's Rule ordered monastic life and shaped the Christian West.

clues.clue: The first three commandments concern the love of this.
clues.explanation: The two tables of the Law order love toward God and love toward neighbor.

clues.clue: This commandment, the fourth, tells us to honor these.
acceptedAnswers: What is your father and your mother
clues.explanation: The fourth commandment opens the second table and grounds the honor owed within family and society.

clues.clue: The Lord summed up the whole Law and the prophets in these two commandments.
clues.answer: love God and love your neighbor
acceptedAnswers: What is love God and love your neighbor
love of God and love of neighbor
to love God and love your neighbor
clues.explanation: On these two commandments hang all the Law and the prophets.

clues.clue: Faith, hope, and charity are called this kind of virtue, because their object is God Himself.
clues.explanation: The theological virtues are infused by God and dispose us to live in relationship with the Trinity.

clues.clue: Prudence, justice, fortitude, and temperance are called this, from the Latin for 'hinge.'
clues.explanation: All the other moral virtues are grouped around these four.

clues.clue: This theological virtue is the greatest, and the form of all the others.
clues.explanation: Charity binds everything together in perfect harmony; without it, nothing profits.

clues.clue: A sin is 'mortal' when it involves grave matter, full knowledge, and this.
clues.explanation: Mortal sin destroys charity in the heart and turns a person away from God.

clues.clue: This kind of grace makes a person pleasing to God and is infused into the soul at Baptism.
clues.explanation: Sanctifying grace is a stable disposition, God's own life dwelling in the soul.

clues.clue: Contrition, confession of sins, and satisfaction are the three acts of the penitent in this sacrament.
clues.explanation: Through the priest's absolution God grants pardon and peace.

clues.clue: Theirs is the kingdom of heaven — the poor in this.
clues.explanation: Poverty of spirit is the humble emptiness that makes room for God.

clues.clue: They will be called children of God — the ones who make this.
clues.explanation: Peacemakers share in the work of the Son who reconciles all things.

clues.clue: They will see God — the ones who are this of heart.
clues.explanation: Purity of heart lets a person see reality, and finally God, as they are.
